why_this_parent: the plan creates the code branch from the current tested optimization SHA. 8aa5cb4 is the first SHA where the launcher can supervise a training phase (cad395e, 66b62af), which is the capability every phase 8 run depends on.

base_model.role: continued pretraining starts here; never the SFT/DPO checkpoint
inherited_limits: the 49,152 tokenizer, not phase 4's selected 32,768 -- a vocabulary cannot be transplanted into trained weights
the released model's dead ShortConv channels, which phase 5's schedules prevent from initialization and cannot revive
base_model.label: Daedalus-Code V1, for both reasons above

baselines_before_adaptation.reading: a 150M base at ~zero execution is expected; both oracles return 1.000 through the identical sandbox, so the zero is the model's answer and not the harness failing to run. MBPP+ syntax validity at 0.238 against HumanEval+'s 1.000 is the headroom to watch: it moves before pass@1 does, and a 250M-token probe gated on pass@1 alone would read every arm as identical zero.

probes_250m.select_on: code BPB and execution pass@1, subject to general retention
probes_250m.stop_if_preregistered_wording: no arm improves code BPB by >=2% or moves execution/syntax signal
probes_250m.stop_if: stop only if NO arm clears EITHER criterion; continue if ANY arm clears EITHER
probes_250m.criterion_a_code_bpb: held-out code BPB improves >=2.0% relative to the untouched base
probes_250m.criterion_b_execution: HumanEval+ or MBPP+ syntax validity improves by >=2.0 points absolute, or either benchmark's pass@1 / pass@1_plus improves by >=1.0 point absolute
probes_250m.disambiguated_when: before any 250M arm had produced a number, and before the code corpus finished building; the timestamp is the `at` field of the phase8-gate-wording decision event in runs/vast-program/events.jsonl, not a clock reading composed here

disambiguation.authority: engineering session, under the plan's rule that a session fixes or justifies an ambiguous gate wording; raised as the phase8-gate-wording gate_ambiguity note in runs/vast-program/events.jsonl
disambiguation.the_ambiguity: 'no arm improves X or moves Y' reads either as stop-if-every-arm-fails-both (loose) or stop-if-no-arm-clears-X-OR-no-arm-moves-Y (strict). The difference is a 1B-token run.
disambiguation.why: the execution/syntax signal was added to this gate as the MORE SENSITIVE alternative to a BPB bar a 250M-token probe may not clear -- see baselines_before_adaptation.reading, which records that a probe gated on pass@1 alone would read every arm as identical zero. Under the strict reading, adding a more sensitive signal makes the gate harder, and would stop a run whose code BPB improved 5% without moving Python syntax validity. That inverts the purpose of the addition.
disambiguation.the_cost_recorded: the loose reading is easier to pass than a BPB-only gate would have been. The criterion B thresholds are what keep it from being passed by noise: an unbounded 'moves' is satisfied by 1 item of 378 (0.26 points), and a gate that cannot return no is not a gate -- the defect the DPO preference gate was repaired for.
disambiguation.why_these_thresholds: 2.0 points of MBPP+ syntax validity is ~8 of 378 items against a 0.238 base, which has the headroom this manifest already names; HumanEval+ syntax validity is 1.000 at base and can only fall, so that half is MBPP+'s in practice. 1.0 point of pass@1 is ~2 of HumanEval+'s 164 and ~4 of MBPP+'s 378, set above one item so a single lucky solve cannot authorise a 1B-token run.
disambiguation.not_decided_here: the winner. select_on says 'subject to general retention' and no retention bound is preregistered for the PROBE stage (only for branch_1b), so probes_250m_verdict ranks the qualifying arms and names best_before_retention; the caller holding the general-side scorecards applies retention and chooses.

branch_1b.continue_if: general BPB regression <=1.5%, five-task mean drop <=1 point, retrieval drop <=2 points at every depth, code metrics improve

extension_2b.only_if: the 1B gate passes and completion is projected before T+136h
extension_2b.how: --init-from the 1B weights, lower LR, fresh WSD, same replay floor
extension_2b.report_as: staged adaptation, not one uninterrupted 3B schedule

dpo.keep_only_if: held-out preference accuracy AND execution pass@1 both improve
dpo.otherwise: the SFT model is the instruct winner and DPO is recorded as rejected

final.execution: HumanEval+/MBPP+ pass@1 and syntax validity must improve over the untouched base

code_split_pct_amendments.why: codeparrot/github-code's parquet revision converted no Rust directory, and the interleaved all-all directory carries Rust at 0.336% of what the licence gate admits -- 23.8 passes of the fallback stream to reach an 8% share, against a one-pass budget. Under the 0.5% floor it is dropped by name rather than carried at a fraction of a percent.

code_split_pct_amendments.kind: deliberate scope choice -- NOT an availability finding
code_split_pct_amendments.authority: USER DECISION, given directly to the operator and recorded verbatim as the phase8-mixture-amendment user_directive in runs/vast-program/events.jsonl
code_split_pct_amendments.why: the code portion is retargeted to Python and JavaScript/TypeScript only, to focus the artifact. These four buckets were reachable: c_cpp and java have their own directories on the revision, go and shell_sql_other cleared the 0.5% floor from the interleaved directory, and corpus headroom verified every one of them SUPPORTED at 250M, 1B and 3B inside the four-epoch cap. Conflating this with the rust drop would misdescribe both -- rust could not be served, these could and were not asked for.
code_split_pct_amendments.why_javascript_typescript_absorbs_it: it has the headroom. At its 14.1% share JS/TS measured 2,531M unique tokens and 0.1 epochs at the 3B gate, so 45% is roughly 0.3 epochs -- far inside the cap.
code_split_pct_amendments.why_python_stays_at_55: the measured plan had drifted Python to 64.4% because all four unreachable buckets were non-Python and the shortfall redistributed proportionally. Both gate benchmarks are Python-only, so that drift was a reporting hazard. Directing the freed share into JavaScript/TypeScript returns Python to exactly its preregistered 55% and removes the eval-language concentration problem rather than deepening it.
code_split_pct_amendments.timing: taken before any corpus was built and before any training number existed; the cost was one CPU re-run of corpus plan and corpus headroom
code_split_pct_amendments.unchanged: the 65/15/20 top-level split, the frozen decontamination index, the admission gate, the by-repository split, the preregistered gates, and the base checkpoint -- none of them depend on which languages are in the mixture

mixture.licences: permissive only, with repository identity, commit/revision and licence recorded per document
